Cautiously optimistic tone: the statement highlights strengthening activity and employment alongside “accommodative” financial conditions, which aligns with New Keynesian guidance that, near the lower bound, commitment and forward guidance can support employment while anchoring expectations (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler; Woodford; DSGE practice at central banks). The continued 0–0.25% policy rate and ongoing asset purchases are consistent with average-inflation-targeting to re-anchor longer-run expectations at 2% and with the credit-channel literature showing that easier financial conditions support real activity (Bernanke–Gertler). 
That said, describing inflation as “transitory” while allowing it to run moderately above 2% introduces the classic Taylor-principle risk if persistence is underestimated (Taylor rule; Cochrane; Orphanides on real-time mismeasurement), though signaling that tapering “may soon be warranted” partly mitigates this concern. Net effect: a mildly positive, but risk-aware stance.
